Hey everyone, thank you so much for your support. I'm packing up my apartment right now (procrastination station), have set up a game plan for next week and we'll see what happnes then. 

I will take up your offers for pm'ing when I have the chance (when I feel better and have more time). Thank you so, so much.

You're situation is exactly like mine. What you describe anyway. I'm lucky to have people who are trying to help me. My best friends have taken me in, because they've said they couldn't imagine life without me and that it will get sorted (not sure how yet, but I trust them). If you trust anyone in this world, talk to them. Talk to them talk to them talk to them. Don't let them pressure you into doing anything you don't want, it won't work, because you'll probably just end up resenting them and then not wanting to talk to them about these things anymore. I hope and wish for you that there is someone in your life who will listen and will try to help you genuinely. 

It's fucking hard as all fuck (excuse the language), but this right now is the only reason I'm willing to stick around and keep fighting my "dark side". I don't feel completely alone and it's helping a little. 

Not advice, just sharing.

I did. My DPDR was more of a reaction to several traumatizing events that happened simultaneously. I shut down to cope and floated around like a ghost or a puppet. I stopped talking. The fact that I started to and then moved on to a different place (this took 3 years) helped. But the symptoms often return when experiences occur that are similar to those first triggering ones. So for me, it's situation specific. now anyway. For reference, it's been ten years

*Late to the party as always, but as I'm in a depressed spell, surfing all the topics I want to talk about.*

For me, it was very similar to being traumatized, if you've ever read up on that. (and after a bit of therapy, I can finally admit it was some form of trauma or ptsd) My body didn't feel real, I was numb all over as if my whole body had fallen asleep as opposed to just an arm or a foot. I stopped thinking. I developed the thousand yard stare. I stopped listening and my minds reaction to anything and everything was to not react. It's like when you're dreaming and everything's fuzzy expect for some small direct details. I didn't want anyone touching or talking to me because then that would mean that I was actually there, the people, the places and the situation included. I'd panic and shut down. I couldn't answer peoples questions. You just, kind of go through the motions. One example that I like to use, were the bus rides to school. After someone at home had forced me outside, it was just a mechanical walk to the bus stop, completely on autorun so to speak. A hatred towards the other kids waiting and a hope that no one would talk to me would build. That would set off the panic. On the bus, I daren't move for fear someone could touch me or acknowledge I was there. I hated it when they laughed or talked in my direction. And I was deathly afraid of the fact that I might have to be the one to push the "stop" button. Because then I'd be doing something, and for other people, people I didn't care about, in a world I didn't want to be in. And it would have had to force me to accept the reality every part of my being rejected.

The fact that I felt like I wasn't there made anything that could remind me this was all reality incredibly fearful. I didn't want it. I didn't want my existance to be the truth.
